title: Throw Food for Anime
pitch: Train your power, hurl food down a lane of anime worlds, and whoever it lures joins your squad and earns for you: the further you throw, the rarer the hero.
core_loop: Train on your dojo gear to raise Power
Pick a food (power, luck and flavour) and charge a throw
The food lands in a zone and lures one character, rolled by rarity, mutation and size
The character joins your plot and earns Yen every second
Spend Yen on better food, dojo gear and plot slots
Rebirth for permanent income and luck, then go again
win_condition: No end state: the goals are filling the Hero Index, climbing the three leaderboards and stacking rebirths.
lose_condition: None. Nothing is ever taken from the player; a bad throw only costs the seconds it took.
out_of_scope: stealing from other plots or any PvP
more than one place or any teleport
pets or followers that walk with the player
any recognisable copyrighted character, name, logo or music

systems.name: DataService
systems.owns: each player's saved profile (session-locked DataStore record, schema version, autosave, release on leave)

systems.name: EconomyService
systems.owns: Yen balance, the per-second income tick, lifetime-earned total, offline earnings on join

systems.name: TrainingService
systems.owns: Power, the active training session, dojo equipment tier

systems.name: ThrowService
systems.owns: throw validation and cooldown, the zone a throw lands in, the rarity/mutation/size roll and its result

systems.name: SquadService
systems.owns: every owned character instance: plot slot or bench, stars, sell, place, pick up, equip best, fuse

systems.name: PlotService
systems.owns: which plot belongs to which player, slot count, and the compact plot state replicated to all clients

systems.name: FoodService
systems.owns: foods owned and the equipped food

systems.name: LuckService
systems.owns: the luck multiplier for a throw: food, depth, perfect, server luck timer, friends, VIP, index, rebirth, lucky throws

systems.name: IndexService
systems.owns: which characters and variants a player has discovered, and zone-completion rewards

systems.name: RebirthService
systems.owns: rebirth tier and the reset it performs

systems.name: RewardsService
systems.owns: daily streak, playtime gifts, codes redeemed, group reward

systems.name: StoreService
systems.owns: ProcessReceipt, pass ownership, product grants, gifting, the paid-random-item policy check

systems.name: LeaderboardService
systems.owns: the three global ordered boards and their cached top lists

systems.name: EventService
systems.owns: Festival Hour timer, server-wide announcements, admin event commands

systems.name: TutorialService
systems.owns: the onboarding step each player has reached

systems.name: TelemetryService
systems.owns: funnel, economy and custom analytics events

systems.name: StateController
systems.owns: the client copy of the player's state and change signals; nothing else reads remotes for state

systems.name: ThrowController
systems.owns: charge input, the throw request, and the flight, landing and reveal sequence for a result

systems.name: SquadRenderController
systems.owns: every character rig in the world: build from templates, place, animate, aura, nameplate, distance culling

systems.name: TrainingController
systems.owns: training input, rep animation and feedback

systems.name: CameraController
systems.owns: the throw follow-camera and its return

systems.name: UIController
systems.owns: which screen is open, open/close transitions, the modal stack; one sub-controller per screen

systems.name: VfxController
systems.owns: playing effects from the VFX kit; every call isolated so a missing effect cannot break gameplay

systems.name: AudioController
systems.owns: sound bank playback, music state, volume settings

systems.name: TutorialController
systems.owns: the objective hint line and guide arrow

plan.overview: Throw Food for Anime. Throw-and-collect idle tycoon (Roblox genre: Simulation / Tycoon). Mobile first, also PC, tablet and gamepad. Ages 9 to 16. Six players per server, R15 avatars, one place.
plan.pitch_and_usp: Hurl food down a lane of anime worlds; whoever it lures joins your squad and earns for you. Why this over the animal game it shares a genre with: (1) the collectibles are full R15 anime-style heroes with idle poses, auras and size variants, not block animals; (2) every catch is a staged reveal (beam colour climbs through the rarities before the hero lands); (3) Cravings: each hero craves a flavour, so food is a choice and not a straight ladder; (4) the charge bar is a zone selector with a perfect window, so the throw has a skill beat; (5) fusion turns duplicates into stars instead of clutter. Everything else (map, art, UI, names, numbers) is our own.
plan.core_concept: 0 min: spawn on your plot, a guide arrow puts you on the throw pad, first throw lands in Sakura Schoolyard and a hero joins the plot and starts earning. 5 min: plot half full, Dango bought, Sandbag bought, first Rare seen, Festival Street unlocked. 30 min: three zones open, first Epic or a Golden mutation, first extra slot, a craving hunt under way for a missing index entry. Tomorrow: offline Yen to claim, day-2 streak reward, Samurai Castle and the first Mythic chance, rebirth visible as the long goal.
plan.player_experience: Fast, loud and generous. A throw resolves in about five seconds and always gives something. The first win is the first catch inside 40 seconds of joining; the first surprise is a rarity beam that keeps climbing. The feeling to protect is 'one more throw'; the feeling to avoid is a modal that stops the next throw (catches never block: they auto-place, auto-swap or go to the bench). Reveals are short for commons (0.8 s), long only for the rare ones, and any tap skips them; a Fast Reveal setting shortens all of them. The Hero Index shows the real chance of each hero at the player's current luck.
plan.audience: Casual collectors first (kids who play Steal a Brainrot, Grow a Garden and the throw-food game), anime fans second, leaderboard chasers third. Short sessions on phones, many per day; friends in the same server compare plots.
plan.market: Looked at on 2026-11-14 (design/research/00, 01, 02). Throw Food For Animals: created 2026-09-18, 215M visits and 426K concurrent at the pull, 94 percent likes, 5-player servers, only two passes and about fifty products; almost all of its store is relative ('N percent of your best animal', 'N minutes of your income'), luck sold per throw and per server. Does well: instant loop, readable goals, relative pricing. Does badly: block art, food is a straight ladder, nothing to do with duplicates, no rebirth or codes; its players complain that luck is opaque, that cutscenes cannot be skipped, that a free player runs out of content in five to six hours, and that each update is more pay-to-win. Each of those is a design target here: odds are shown, every reveal is skippable, rebirth extends the ladder, and nothing sold is unobtainable by play except cosmetics-grade premium heroes. Anime entries in the genre are small (World3 Throw an Anime Coin: 1.1M visits, 2K peak), so the anime throw angle is open. Big anime games on the platform are combat games, which shows the audience exists. Risk read: recognisable anime IP is removed on DMCA notice and not reopened, and the free 'anime character' models on the Creator Store are mostly re-uploads of copyrighted characters from deleted accounts, so the roster is original.
plan.mechanics: Movement: stock R15, no combat. Throw: stand on the throw pad, hold to charge, release; charge picks the zone (marks on the bar), the top 8 percent is a perfect release (+10 percent luck). Landing zone = furthest zone whose PowerReq <= Power x food PowerMult x charge. Roll: rarity by zone table weights scaled by luck, then mutation, then size; a craved flavour triples that hero's weight. Catch: reveal, hero dashes home, auto-places (free slot, else swaps out the weakest if better, else bench, else auto-sell). Income: every hero on a slot pays base x rarity x mutation x size x stars each second, times pass, rebirth and event multipliers. Training: hold-free auto reps on the plot's dojo gear, Power per rep by gear tier. Economy sinks: food, gear, slots, rebirth. Squad: place, pick up, sell, equip best, fuse three identical into +1 star. Luck: food, depth into the zone, perfect, server luck, friends, VIP, index, rebirth, lucky throws. Meta: Hero Index, rebirth, daily streak, playtime gifts, codes, leaderboards, Festival Hour, server-wide rare-catch banners. Full formulas: design/plan/01-game-design.md.
plan.progression: Short (minutes): next food, next gear, fill the plot, next zone gate. Medium (hours): Samurai Castle, Hero City, Spirit Realm, first Legendary, first Mythic, complete a zone index, max slots. Long (days and weeks): rebirth tiers 1 to 10 (each +50 percent income and +10 percent luck), golden and titan variants in the index, leaderboard rank, new zones from updates. Measured pacing for a no-boost player (tools/balance_sim.py): zone 2 at 2 min, zone 3 at 14 min, zone 4 at 51 min, zone 5 at 2 h 44, zone 6 at 7 h 18, first rebirth ready at 15 h.
plan.content: 48 throw-caught heroes (6 zones x 8) plus 8 premium heroes (6 in the summon scroll, 1 starter pack, 1 limited). 7 rarities (Secret reserved for events). 4 mutations, 3 sizes, 3 star levels. 12 foods in 4 flavours (8 from CC0 packs, 4 built with the 3D skill). 8 dojo gear tiers. 6 zones. 1 hub with food cart, sell booth, summon shrine, daily chest and three leaderboards. 6 plots. No enemies. The full roster with looks is config.Characters.
plan.world: One straight world. Hub and a row of six plots at the start; each plot faces its own 40-stud lane; the six lanes run in parallel through six zone bands of 220 studs each, with an arch between bands showing the Power needed. Sakura Schoolyard (start, PowerReq 0), Festival Street (200), Ninja Village (3K), Samurai Castle (70K), Hero City (2M), Spirit Realm (36M). Players can walk the lanes and other plots; nothing there can hurt or be taken. Later zones are appended to the far end by data.
plan.story: One line, never in the way: the Anime Worlds are hungry, and the best cook-thrower in town can recruit anyone. No dialogue beyond tutorial hints and NPC shop greetings.
plan.ui_ux: Style 'Manga Pop': deep indigo panels with a thick white keyline and offset comic shadow, coral-to-yellow header ribbons with halftone dots, chunky rounded type with dark stroke, rarity colours everywhere. Screens: HUD, ThrowMeter, FoodShop, Squad, HeroIndex, Store, OfflineEarnings, Reveal, Rebirth, DailyRewards, PlaytimeGifts, Codes, Settings, TrainingBar, Nameplate, Leaderboards, Toasts, Announcement, TutorialHint, ServerLuckBar, SummonOdds, SlotSign. Common action cost: throw = one hold and release, 0 menus; equip food = 2 taps; sell a hero = 2 taps; equip best = 2 taps. Touch targets at least 56 px at 720p, safe-area aware, every panel opens with a 0.18 s scale-and-fade and closes on outside tap. Detail: design/plan/05-ui-ux.md.
plan.tutorial: Beat by beat, all skippable by simply doing it: (1) 0:00 camera on your plot, hint 'Step on the pad' with a ground arrow; (2) 0:08 hint 'Hold to throw', bar pulses; (3) 0:15 first throw, guaranteed Uncommon, reveal plays, hero dashes home; (4) 0:30 'Throw again' until three heroes; (5) 1:10 'Buy Dango' arrow to the food cart, shop opens with Dango highlighted; (6) 1:40 'Train to throw further' arrow to the dojo gear, ten reps; (7) 2:10 gate arch for Festival Street pulses with the Power needed; (8) on first zone-2 landing, Zone_Unlock effect and the hint line retires. Each step is logged to the onboarding funnel.
plan.art_direction: Bright stylised anime world, not blocky: smooth low-poly props with flat colour and soft gradient textures, saturated key colour per zone, Future lighting with warm sun, bloom and a little colour grading. Characters are standard R15 rigs dressed as whole looks, anime hair and faces, one signature accessory, never more than six accessories. Every hero must be readable at 60 studs by silhouette and rarity colour of its pedestal. Mutations are auras, not recolours. Props are real meshes (free packs first, built with the 3D skill where no free asset fits); no stand-in boxes. No copyrighted character, logo or pattern.
plan.audio: Music: one upbeat festival loop at home (music_home), a faster variant during Festival Hour. Ambience per zone under the follow-cam. SFX roles: UI click/open/close/error, buy, coin tick, throw charge and whoosh, perfect ding, food land, reveal drumroll, five reveal stings rising with rarity, index new, train hit, power up, slot unlock, rebirth, summon open, daily claim, server luck, munch, dash. All from the Creator Store audio library by id, length measured in Studio.
plan.technical_architecture: Rojo project, Knit for lifecycle only, every remote declared in Net.luau, all tunables generated from this file into src/shared/Config (gen_config.py), all rules as pure Core modules with Lune specs: Throw, Roll, Luck, Income, Training, Costs, Rebirth, Fusion, Index, Offline, Rewards, Receipt, Format, Schema. Server services and client controllers are listed in systems. The server never spawns character rigs: it replicates a compact plot state and each client builds rigs from baked templates in ReplicatedStorage.Assets. Roblox services used: DataStoreService (profiles, ordered boards), MemoryStoreService (not at launch), MarketplaceService, PolicyService, AnalyticsService, MessagingService (global announcements), TextChatService, ContentProvider, TweenService, CollectionService. StreamingEnabled on. Detail: design/plan/02-architecture.md.
plan.data_saving: One profile per player, session-locked, autosave every 120 s, save on leave and BindToClose. Persisted: schema version, Yen, lifetime Yen, Power, rebirth tier, foods owned and equipped, gear tier, slot count, every owned hero (id, mutation, size, stars, slot or bench), index, lucky throws, passes cache, receipts already granted (last 100 ids), daily streak and last claim day, playtime gifts claimed today, codes redeemed, tutorial step, settings, stats for boards, last-seen timestamp for offline earnings. If load fails: the player is kicked with a retry message rather than given a blank profile. If a save fails: retried with backoff, and purchases are only acknowledged to Roblox after the grant is in a saved profile. Schema migrations are pure functions with specs.
plan.security: The client sends intents only. Throw: server checks the player is on their own pad, cooldown, charge in [0.2, 1], food is owned; the server alone computes landing zone and the roll. Buy: server checks price against Config and balance. Squad moves: server checks ownership and slot bounds. Training: server counts reps on its own clock, the client cannot report Power. Store: grants only inside ProcessReceipt with idempotent receipt ids. Rate limits per remote. No remote takes a number the server could compute itself.
plan.multiplayer: Six players per server, one plot each, assigned on join and freed on leave (the leaver's heroes vanish from the world; their data is already saved). Everything a player owns is theirs alone: no shared state except server luck, Festival Hour and banners. Server luck bought by one player helps all six, which is the social reason to stay in a server.
plan.monetisation: Things a player would happily buy because they speed up what they are already doing. Passes: 2x Yen (99), 2x Training (149), VIP (249: +15 percent luck, +2 slots, tag), Auto Throw (199), Lucky Aura (299: 1.5x luck), Big Bench (79). Products: lucky throws (9, 39, 149), server luck step (29, stacks 2x 4x 8x), Yen packs priced in minutes of your own income (29, 99, 299), training skips (39, 149), 2x offline claim (39), summon scrolls with disclosed odds (79, 199, 599), starter pack (49, once), one limited hero (399), gift versions of the two 2x passes. Summon scrolls are paid random items: odds shown before purchase, PolicyService checked, and where restricted the scroll is hidden and the same heroes are offered at fixed prices. Product ids are minted in section 5.
plan.economy: Yen. Enters: hero income per second, offline earnings (50 percent rate, 8 hour cap), selling heroes (30 s of their income), daily and playtime rewards, index rewards, codes, Yen packs. Leaves: foods, dojo gear, plot slots, rebirth. Power. Enters: training reps, training skips. Leaves: reset on rebirth. Lucky throws. Enter: daily streak, group reward, codes, store. Leave: one per armed throw. All prices and curves are in config and were tuned with tools/balance_sim.py against config.Pacing.
plan.retention: Tomorrow: offline Yen waiting, the next streak day (lucky throws on days 3, 5 and 7), a zone gate left half-trained. This week: index completion per zone, rebirth, Festival Hour every 30 minutes, a weekly content drop (one zone of eight heroes is a data edit plus eight looks), codes on update days, limited heroes. Every session ends with something about to unlock.
plan.social: Three global leaderboards in the hub (most Yen earned, most heroes caught, rarest catch). Server-wide banner when anyone catches Legendary or better. Friend bonus: +10 percent luck per friend in the server, up to 30. Server luck is shared. Gifting of the two 2x passes. Group reward chest. Trading and stealing are out of scope.
